quests.partialSentence: This software update will ____ how the app handles notifications.
quests.hint: Think about the verb form, meaning 'to influence something.'
quests.explanation: 'Affect' is normally used as a verb meaning 'to influence,' fitting how the update changes the app.

quests.partialSentence: The full ____ of this update won't be clear until next month.
quests.hint: Think about the noun form, meaning 'a result.'
quests.explanation: 'Effect' is normally used as a noun meaning 'a result,' fitting the outcome of the update.

quests.partialSentence: There are ____ bugs in this version compared to the last one.
quests.hint: 'Bugs' is a countable plural noun, so think about the quantifier used with countable nouns.
quests.explanation: 'Fewer' is used with countable plural nouns like 'bugs,' while 'less' is used with uncountable nouns.

quests.partialSentence: Lack of sleep can seriously ____ your concentration during the day.
quests.hint: This word functions as a verb here, meaning 'to have an influence on.'
quests.explanation: 'Affect' functions as a verb meaning 'to influence,' fitting how sleep impacts concentration.

quests.partialSentence: Doctors are still studying the long-term ____ of this treatment.
quests.hint: Think about the plural noun form, meaning 'results.'
quests.explanation: 'Effects' is the plural noun form meaning 'results,' fitting multiple outcomes of a treatment.

quests.partialSentence: I've been eating ____ sugar lately to improve my health.
quests.hint: 'Sugar' is an uncountable noun, so think about the quantifier used with uncountable nouns.
quests.explanation: 'Less' is used with uncountable nouns like 'sugar,' while 'fewer' is used with countable nouns.

quests.partialSentence: We regret to inform you that the show ____ due to unforeseen circumstances.
quests.hint: Think about the more formal passive structure typically used in official announcements.
quests.explanation: Formal announcements typically use the passive voice instead of casual phrasing like 'got cancelled.'

quests.partialSentence: Patrons are kindly requested ____ from using mobile phones during the performance.
quests.hint: Think about the formal structure 'request someone to do something.'
quests.explanation: Formal requests use the structure 'request + person + to + verb': 'requested to refrain.'

quests.partialSentence: In formal writing, 'a lot of people came' is often rephrased as ____.
quests.hint: Think about which option uses formal vocabulary instead of casual expressions.
quests.explanation: Formal writing favors precise vocabulary like 'numerous attendees were present' over casual phrases such as 'a bunch of people.'

quests.partialSentence: We would be grateful if you ____ confirm your attendance by Friday.
quests.hint: Think about the more formal, polite modal often used in written requests.
quests.explanation: 'Could' sounds more formal and polite than 'can' in written requests, especially in business correspondence.

quests.partialSentence: Please be advised that the office ____ closed for the public holiday.
quests.hint: Think about the more formal future form typically used in official notices.
quests.explanation: Formal notices typically use 'will be' rather than the more casual 'going to be' or 'gonna be.'

quests.partialSentence: In a formal email, 'I wanted to ask you something' is often rewritten as ____.
options: I was wondering if you could help
quests.correctAnswer: I was wondering if you could help
quests.hint: Think about which option uses polite, formal phrasing appropriate for written correspondence.
quests.explanation: Formal correspondence favors polite, indirect phrasing like 'I was wondering if you could help' over casual expressions.

quests.partialSentence: We need to ____ our spending habits if we want to save more this year.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to reduce something gradually.
quests.explanation: 'Cut down on' means to reduce the amount of something, fitting spending less money.

quests.partialSentence: It took me a while to ____ the new neighborhood after moving here.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to become familiar and comfortable with something.
quests.explanation: 'Get used to' means to become familiar and comfortable with a new situation.

quests.partialSentence: I finally managed to ____ all the paperwork for my new apartment.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to organize or resolve something successfully.
quests.explanation: 'Sort out' means to organize or successfully deal with a problem or task.

quests.partialSentence: She had to ____ a lot of extra work to catch up after being absent.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to do something you missed in order to be up to date.
quests.explanation: 'Catch up on' means to do something you missed in order to reach the same level as others.

quests.partialSentence: The professor decided to ____ the exam date due to the public holiday.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to postpone or delay something.
quests.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay an event to a later time.

quests.partialSentence: It's important to ____ a good relationship with your classmates.
quests.hint: Think about the phrasal verb meaning to develop something gradually over time.
quests.explanation: 'Build up' means to gradually develop or strengthen something, such as a relationship.

quests.partialSentence: The deadline was ____ tight that nobody had time for lunch.
quests.hint: Think about the structure 'so + adjective + that' used for emphasis.
quests.explanation: 'So' is followed directly by an adjective in emphasis structures: 'so tight that.'

quests.partialSentence: It was ____ difficult project that the whole team had to work overtime.
quests.hint: Think about the structure 'such a/an + adjective + noun + that' used for emphasis.
quests.explanation: 'Such a' is followed by an adjective and a singular noun in emphasis structures: 'such a difficult project.'

quests.partialSentence: She gave ____ a convincing presentation that the client signed immediately.
quests.hint: Think about the structure 'such + adjective + plural/uncountable noun + that.'
quests.explanation: 'Such' is followed by an adjective and noun without an article when emphasizing a quality, here before 'a' as part of 'such a.'

quests.partialSentence: The view from the hotel balcony was ____ breathtaking that we just stood there in silence.
quests.hint: This emphasis pattern places the adjective directly after 'so.'
quests.explanation: 'So' is followed directly by an adjective in this emphasis structure: 'so breathtaking that.'

quests.partialSentence: It was ____ long flight that we watched four movies just to pass the time.
quests.hint: This emphasis pattern needs an article before the adjective and singular noun.
quests.explanation: 'Such a' precedes an adjective and singular noun for emphasis: 'such a long flight.'

quests.partialSentence: We had ____ amazing experience that we're already planning to return next year.
quests.hint: Think about the structure 'such an + adjective + noun + that,' since 'amazing' starts with a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: 'Such an' is used before a vowel-sound adjective and noun for emphasis: 'such an amazing experience.'

quests.partialSentence: Had I known about the surprise party, I ____ acted differently.
quests.hint: This is an inverted third conditional ('Had I known' = 'If I had known'), so the main clause uses 'would have.'
quests.explanation: Inverting 'if' to 'had' creates a formal third conditional; the main clause still uses 'would have' + past participle.

quests.partialSentence: Rarely ____ such a close-knit family as the one next door.
quests.hint: Placing 'Rarely' at the front of a sentence for emphasis reverses the usual word order.
quests.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'Rarely' at the front of a sentence require inversion: 'have I seen.'

quests.partialSentence: It was my aunt ____ taught me how to bake bread from scratch.
quests.hint: Think about the cleft sentence structure emphasizing a specific person.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentences with 'It was...who' emphasize a specific person responsible for an action.

quests.partialSentence: Had the store offered free returns, more customers ____ shopped there.
quests.hint: This is an inverted third conditional, so the main clause uses 'would have.'
quests.explanation: Inverted third conditionals keep the usual main clause form: 'would have' + past participle.

quests.partialSentence: Not only ____ the price drop, but the quality also improved.
quests.hint: Beginning a sentence with 'Not only' forces the auxiliary verb before the subject.
quests.explanation: After 'Not only' at the front of a sentence, the auxiliary inverts with the subject: 'did we notice.'

quests.partialSentence: It was the long queue ____ made us decide to shop online instead.
quests.hint: Think about the cleft sentence structure emphasizing a specific cause.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentences with 'It was...that' use 'that' to emphasize a cause, here the long queue.
